title: Dashboard filter bar and condition editors still send = / $in on a multi-value field, which the server refuses (follow-up to #35559)
body:
repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CZiaBg6rk7dpy1s9Me

Filing gate: ① the part of #35559 its PR cannot reach inside its file surface. PR #35991 (#35559) makes the list's quick filter and the shared advanced filter builder offer 包含 / 不包含 / 为空 / 不为空 for multi-value fields, through one helper `jsonColumnFilterOperators(field)` in `@object-ui/components`. Two more surfaces were found by reading, not measured. Suggested grade: p2. ⛔ Not a claim; triage sets lane and grade.

## By reading (origin/main, not measured)

- **Dashboard filter bar.** A select / lookup global filter bound to a multi-value field is lowered to bare equality or `$in` by `ui/packages/core/src/…/dashboard-filters.ts` `buildFilterCondition`. The server refuses both on a JSON column (400 INVALID_FILTER; `packages/core/src/utils/json-column-operator-refusal.ts`). No showcase dashboard binds such a field today, so the dev could not measure it.
- **Condition editors that build filter fields without `multiple`.** `FilterConditionField` (`@object-ui/fields`) and the metadata-admin / Studio condition rows (ConditionBuilder, flow-edge-condition-rows, dataset filter) pass no `multiple`. So a select / lookup / user field with `multiple: true` keeps its single-value operators there. multiselect, checkboxes and tags are already fixed by type through the shared builder. Whether the code that evaluates those conditions refuses these operators was not measured.

## Done when

- A dashboard global filter bound to a multi-value field sends `contains` (one member per condition, `or` for any-of), and the dashboard answers with rows instead of a refusal. Pinned with a fixture dashboard.
- The condition editors pass `multiple` to the shared builder, so `multiple: true` select / lookup / user fields offer only what their evaluator accepts. Measure the evaluator first: if it is not the JSON-column refusal, state what it accepts.

Dedupe: issue search `dashboard filter multi-value equality`, `buildFilterCondition multiselect`, `FilterConditionField multiple` → only #35559.
